sentences.text:
Petitioner has filed this writ petition seeking for the following reliefs :-
"i) Issue writ of certiorari quashing the General Award bearing No.KIADB /LAQ/52/2023-24 dated 10.04.2023 passed by the Respondent No.3 in respect of land in Sy.No.21/2P measuring 3 Acres 8 Guntas of land situated at Chapparadahalli Village, Kundana Hobli, Devanahalli Taluk, Bangalore Rural District, insofar as the petitioner is concerned, which is produced as Annexure-D.
ii) Issue any suitable order, direction or writ in the nature of mandamus directing the respondent herein to consider the case of the petitioner as per Section 29(2) of the KIADB Act, and by directing Respondent to withdraw the general award amount deposited in the reference court.

2. Sri Sharan N. Majage, learned counsel for petitioner submitted that, petitioner was owner of land in Sy.no.21/2P, measuring 03 Acres and 8 guntas of land situated at Chapparadahalli village,
Kundana Hobli, Devanahalli Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District.

Respondent no.3 had initiated acquisition proceedings in respect petitioner's land under NC: 2023:KHC:44992 Preliminary notification dated 09.06.2010 and Final notification dated 25.05.2022 for purpose of ITIR Project.

It was submitted that though petitioner was entitled to higher compensation under consent award,
without offering opportunity to avail same, General Award was passed, constrained petitioner to file this writ petition.

sentences.text: On other hand, Sri Manjunath V Rayappa, learned AGA for respondent no.1 and Sri H.L. Pradeep Kumar, learned counsel for respondents no.2 and 3 submitted that respondent no.3 was constrained to pass general award, as petitioner failed to substantiate her case by producing records.
It was submitted that, respondent no.3 would consider representation in accordance with law, within reasonable period.

4. Heard learned counsel and perused writ petition record.
5.
From above, in this petition neither facts nor law are disputed.

It is seen under similar circumstances, this Court has set-aside General Award and directed respondents to consider petitioner's case for passing consent award and failure to provide opportunity to accept compensation under consent award which was higher than under General award.

Consequently, writ petition is disposed of and General Award bearing No.KIADB /LAQ/52/2023-24 dated 10.04.2023 at Annexure-D, passed by respondent No.3 in respect of petitioner's land in Sy.no.21/2P, measuring 03 Acres 8 Guntas of land situated at Chapparadahalli Village, Kundana Hobli, Devanahalli Taluk, Bangalore Rural District, is quashed.
Respondent no.3 is directed to consider petitioner's case for passing consent award under Section 29(2) of KIAD Act within two months.
Needless to observe that direction issued shall not be construed as a positive direction but only as a direction to consider case on its own merit in accordance with law.
However, it is made clear that if there were found to be any dispute relating to title of lands in question, General Award passed shall stand revived.
Respondent no.3 is permitted to withdraw compensation, if any, deposited before Reference Court.
